world._procedural_note: true generates the world from the seed: sites proposed by the land, named from their own numbers, connected by roads. false uses data/settlements/settlements.json, the authored starting region, which stays useful for tests that want a known map.

roads._comment: The road network as a living thing. A link between two settlements carries a tier; the priced grid, the eta and the walking pace all read the tier's speed bonus. A settlement founded later links itself to its nearest neighbour as a dirt road - 'a very small bonus'. Traffic (world units walked on the link) raises a tier once upgrade_traffic is met; a link nobody has used for decay_days_per_tier of game days falls one tier, and can eventually be roadless again, which takes years: 'roadless, it takes years though, so I doubt it will ever happen.' A road never simply runs over water: a crossing no wider than bridge_max_span becomes a bridge, and a wider lake bends the road around it.

battle._comment: Battle simulation settings. tick_rate is the fixed simulation step the runtime advances the fight at: frames are accumulated and whole ticks are run, so one tick is always 1/tick_rate seconds and the same seed fights the same battle whatever the machine renders at. The owner set sixty on 2026-09-18 and asked to try thirty later the same night, watching what the fight and the map read like at half the rate; every tick-counted rule below halved with it, so the same rule still means the same number of seconds. A tick is a design decision, not a rendering one.

terrain._comment: Battlefield terrain generation. The same terrain_seed, field size, biome and generation_version always produce the same battlefield. Bump generation_version when the generation rules change, so old seeds are not silently reinterpreted. The knobs here are the ones that are the same in every country; everything a particular country does - its landforms, its soils, its vegetation, its movement drags - lives in data/terrain/biomes.json.

_fields.generation_version: bumped when the generation rules change
_fields.biome: which country the field is grown as (see data/terrain/biomes.json)
_fields.blend_biome: a second country mixed into it across a transition band; empty means one country throughout
_fields.blend_width_cells: how wide that band is, in cells
_fields.elevation_amplitude: world units of relief at roughness 1.0, before the biome's own amplitude multiplier
_fields.detail_amplitude: world units of restrained small-scale variation laid over the landforms
_fields.cliff_slope: rise over run at which ground becomes a cliff: 1.0 is forty-five degrees
_fields.rough_slope: rise over run at which ground becomes rough
_fields.max_traversable_slope: steeper than this and no formation crosses, whatever the type says
_fields.woods_vegetation: vegetation density at which ground becomes woods
_fields.mud_wetness: wetness at which low ground becomes mud
_fields.high_ground_fraction: the fraction of the field that lies below the high-ground line: 0.8 makes the highest fifth of the field high ground
_fields.water_fraction: how far below the ground around it a cell must stand to hold water, as a fraction of the field's height span
_fields.variant_strength: how far a cell may go toward one ground variant: capped below 1 so no cell is entirely one thing
_fields.rock_vegetation: rockiness at which ground becomes rough
_fields.visual_pixels_per_unit: resolution of the baked ground and overlay maps the view draws

formation._comment: Generic formation tuning. Per-formation-type shape lives in data/formations/formation_types.json; these are the numbers shared by every formation.

recruitment.starting_equipment_note: equipment arrives with the inventory system

trade._comment: Caravans (D-139). caravan_count is how many the roads carry; speed_multiplier is the caravan's pace as a fraction of the player's own walk and is hard-capped at 1.0 (a caravan is never faster than the player); cargo_speed_penalty_per_good slows a loaded cart further; max_route_units is the longest leg worth planning; guards_min/max size each caravan's guard party; meeting_radius is how close the player is when traders have their say; meeting_cooldown_hours is how long they keep their distance afterwards; markup is what a crate costs over the catalogue value when bought off a cart.
